PullRequest.Title: Update sweeper-fix skill to v6: agent-ready tiers, plan-first mode, plan file
PullRequest.Body:
**TL;DR** — The VS Code Sweeper reviews the open backlog nightly and, for issues it can diagnose from the source, writes a brief an agent can act on. This skill is how a maintainer turns that brief into a draft PR from their own checkout, under their own identity, with the sweeper never writing to this repo. Until now the lane only covered small, fully diagnosed bugs; most issues worth an agent's time instead need a human decision first (which of two designs, what the boundary is, whether the repro even holds). v6 adds that second tier: for those issues the skill writes a plan **with** the maintainer and stops for approval before touching code, and for the fully diagnosed ones it goes straight to the change as before. Both paths end with the change validated against a written plan, so a plausible fix for the wrong problem is caught before review. The matching Implement / Plan buttons in vscode-tools are in microsoft/vscode-tools#1114.

Skill v6 (generated from the vscodesweeper repo's template; getting started: https://egamma.github.io/vscodesweeper-state/fix-skill.html).

The sweeper's review records now carry an **agent-readiness tier** instead of the boolean fix flag: `implement` (the review did the diagnosis — confirmed defect, bounded change, a named validation) or `plan` (the goal is clear but a design or diagnosis is open). The skill reads the tier and runs in the matching mode; the old `autoFixable: true` records still count as implement.

- **One skill, two modes.** `implement` goes straight to the change, as v5 did. `plan-first` puts the review's open decisions to you first (with a recommendation each, never guessed), reproduces before designing when the review could not confirm the bug, writes the plan with you and **stops for your approval before touching any code**. You can ask for plan-first on an implement record; the reverse is never allowed.
- **A plan file, never committed.** Both modes write `.sweeper/plans/issue-<n>.md` (Behavior / Approach / Validation / Open decisions), seeded from the review's brief, and add `.sweeper/` to `.git/info/exclude` — no `.gitignore` change, works in worktrees.
- **Validate against the plan.** Before showing the diff, the skill checks it statement by statement: every Behavior statement covered by a test, nothing changed outside the plan's boundary, every named test fails before and passes after, no open decision left. Then the **full diff is its own approval step** — never folded into the validate summary.
- **PR body.** Adds `Sweeper mode: implement | plan-first` under the seeded-by line and the plan in a collapsed `<details>` block, so reviewers get the map of the change.
- Reads the review's brief in its new two-part form (Behavior / Trace) and still accepts older records' `Fix prompt`.

Unchanged from v5: the strict trigger (only explicit sweeper requests), the graceful hand-back when no record exists, the live gates (issue open, no `security` label, no open PR referencing the issue, staleness warning, re-checked before push), the clean-checkout requirement, explicit-path staging, and the draft-only PR the maintainer owns.

Both modes were exercised end to end on the sweeper's sandbox repo before this update (plan-first: egamma/sweeper-sandbox#18; implement: egamma/sweeper-sandbox#19).

Scenarios.Scenario: Implement-mode sweeper run from record fetch through draft PR creation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Local precondition checks, three live GitHub reads, plan-file creation, implementation, baseline/fixed validation, plan/diff review, gate recheck, push, and PR creation are serial prerequisites. The newly added plan write and diff-stat comparison are on the critical path but bounded to one issue and one narrow PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch one sweeper record with gh api
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per invocation; no collection fan-out or cache is described.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The v5 workflow fetched the same single record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before readiness and brief parsing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch issue state/labels/update time and search open PRs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two GitHub queries initially, then the issue/PR gates are repeated once before shipping; cardinality is constant per issue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial and pre-ship live gates existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial gate before work and before public push.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append .sweeper/ to .git/info/exclude and write one issue plan
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small plan file per invoked issue plus at most one exclude-file update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No plan file or exclude update was required.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run each planned test against failing and fixed states
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with the number of Behavior statements/tests in one bounded PR, but v5 already required the validation test to fail before and pass after.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior workflow likewise required its added validation test to run both before and after the fix; v6 formalizes coverage for each behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tests must complete before presenting the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inspect git diff --stat and then render the full git diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two local scans of the single narrow PR diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The full diff had to be shown before push, but there was no separate plan-boundary diff-stat check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one bounded summary scan before the already-required full diff review.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Push one branch and create one draft PR
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One push and one PR creation per successful invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: v5 performed the same push and draft-PR creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One issue, one plan, a narrowly bounded set of changed files, and the Behavior/test statements for that issue.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The workflow is deliberately serial around gates, implementation, validation, approvals, and shipping; no changed loop or aggregate concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used. GitHub state is intentionally refreshed before shipping; local plan and diff work are not repeated on cache misses.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete instruction diff: the only new local work is one plan artifact and one diff-stat pass; network cardinality and baseline/fixed testing are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact test-suite duration and diff size vary by issue, but the newly added work is bounded and the dominant run-before/run-after test pattern was already required.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added filesystem and diff-summary work is constant or bounded by the intentionally narrow PR and does not establish meaningful latency, I/O, CPU, or retention growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Plan-first sweeper run with unresolved design or unconfirmed reproduction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same initial GitHub gates precede interactive decision resolution. When reproduction is unconfirmed, reproduction/test work must complete before designing; maintainer approval then gates implementation, validation, diff approval, and shipping.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch one record, one issue, and search open PRs, then refresh gates before shipping
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Constant per issue, with the live issue/PR checks refreshed once before shipping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These gates existed in implement-only v5; plan-first extends them to a newly supported scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial gate around the potentially long approval pause.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reproduce the defect or run a failing test before plan design
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one bounded reproduction attempt for a plan-tier issue whose record is not already reproduced; no per-item fan-out is prescribed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plan-tier issues were unsupported, so there was no corresponding v5 plan-first path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and revise one excluded plan file as decisions are answered
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small file per issue, revised only with bounded maintainer decisions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous skill had no plan-first workflow or plan artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Plan must be complete and approved before implementation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of open decisions and Behavior statements for one issue, explicitly bounded to a single reviewable PR slice.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All decisions, reproduction, approval, implementation, and shipping are sequenced; there is no changed concurrent subprocess or network burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A reproduced/source-reproducible record skips the reproduction step. The plan persists locally for the issue but is a single excluded file; no unbounded in-process cache or retained object graph is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the new mode adds serial reproduction and plan work, but equally high confidence that there is no before/after regression for this previously unsupported scenario and that scope is explicitly bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reproduction and tests can be slow depending on subsystem, but this is required work for a newly enabled workflow rather than increased cost on a previously supported plan-first path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new costs are intrinsic to the newly supported plan-first capability, bounded per issue, and do not create scaling fan-out, unbounded retention, or a concurrency burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invocation where no sweeper record exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One failed record lookup is followed by one pinned issue fetch and the normal non-sweeper implementation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attempt record fetch, then fetch the issue from microsoft/vscode
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two serial requests for the single issue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: v5 used the same record lookup and fallback issue fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The failed lookup precedes fallback issue analysis.

Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; the absent record is queried once in this invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from unchanged commands in the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency varies, but request cardinality is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed file and all diff pages. The PR adds a bounded per-issue plan artifact, optional plan-first reproduction, and a local diff-stat validation pass, while preserving existing GitHub request cardinality, baseline/fixed test semantics, and serial shipping gates. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
